title: Using a Number Line for Length

steps.body: The number line is a ruler that never ends: lengths become jumps from zero, joins chain forward, and differences appear as gaps.
steps.narration: The number line is a ruler that never ends: lengths become jumps from zero, joins chain forward, and differences appear as gaps.

widget.prompt: A 34 cm piece as a jump from zero — then chain a 20 cm piece: two more ten-hops.

commonLandings.feedback: One ten of the second piece — its whole 20 cm belongs in the chain.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 10. From 34, 2 hops land on 54.
widget.successFeedback: 54 — two pieces chained on the endless ruler, their join read at the landing.

predict.prompt: On the line, a length is best shown as…

options.label: A jump of that many units

predict.reveal: A dot marks a place; a LENGTH covers ground — and covering ground is a jump.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2p line model.
invariants: Lengths compare only from a shared start, join by placing end to end, and split so the parts rebuild the whole exactly for g2p line model.
misconceptions: Comparing unaligned ends, reading a ruler's end mark as a length, or letting a total drift from the sum of its parts.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What would have to change about the pieces for the total or the gap to come out differently?

widget.prompt: Maggie joins a 45 cm ribbon and a 30 cm ribbon. Which number-line drawing shows the join?

options.label: Jump 45, then 30 more, to land on 75
options.feedback: Correct — each piece is its own forward jump, and the landing 75 reads the joined total.

options.label: Dots at 45 and at 30, with no jumps between
options.feedback: Dots mark positions; joined lengths need jumps laid end to end from zero.

options.label: Start at 45 and jump back 30
options.feedback: Jumping back subtracts — that drawing shows 45 − 30 = 15, not a join.

options.label: One jump of 45, ignoring the 30
options.feedback: The 30 cm piece vanished; both pieces must appear as their own jumps.

hints: Place the pieces end to end.
The total is the far end.

widget.prompt: A pencil stretches from the 4 cm mark to the 10 cm mark on a ruler. How long is it?

commonErrors.feedback: That read the END mark as the length — a start away from zero must be subtracted off.
Adding the marks measures nothing on a ruler; the length is the span BETWEEN them.

widget.prompt: Two ropes join: 16 cm, then 22 cm. Which jumps show this on a number line?

options.label: Jump 16, then 22, land on 38
options.feedback: Correct — the ropes chain head to tail, and the landing spot reads the joined total.

options.label: Dots at 16 and at 22, no jumps
options.feedback: Dots only mark spots; joined lengths need jumps laid end to end from zero.

options.label: Jump 16, then hop back 22
options.feedback: Hopping back takes length away — joining ropes sends the second jump forward.

options.label: One jump of 22 and nothing more
options.feedback: That drawing drops the 16 entirely; both ropes must appear as their own jumps.
